headline.technical: AP reported the S&P 500 tumbled 4.4% as AI stocks sold off after the Democratic midterm sweep; the Nasdaq Composite closed -5.52% and the VIX at 28.18.
headline.layman: US shares fell sharply as investors worried Democrats could slow the AI building boom. AP said the S&P 500 fell 4.4%.

global.title: AI rout hits Wall Street after Democratic midterm sweep

status.technical: AP reported the S&P 500 fell 4.4% (-4.36% on the close) and the Nasdaq Composite closed -5.52%. The VIX closed at 28.18, 69.66% higher on the day. The Financial Times reported Wall Street shed $3.2tn; CNBC reported the Magnificent 7 lost $1 trillion.
status.layman: US stocks dropped hard on Thursday. AP said the S&P 500 fell 4.4%. The Financial Times said Wall Street lost $3.2tn. Investors fear that Democrats, now in control of Congress, will curb AI data centres.

consequence.technical: The FT reported newly elected officials have pledged to curb data centre construction, and CNBC reported calls for a data center moratorium. If limits on the AI build-out materialise, AI-linked demand and earnings expectations could be reassessed, which is the worry Bloomberg described behind the slide.
consequence.layman: If lawmakers do limit data centres, companies building AI may spend less or wait. That is why investors sold first. The notes describe pledges and calls for limits, not a new law.

impact.technical: Chip and AI names bore the brunt: Nvidia -9.26% and Broadcom -10.43% on the day; Bloomberg reported Korean chip stocks sank 10% pre-market. Mint reported Treasuries rose on haven demand, and WSJ reported D.R. Horton, PulteGroup and Lennar outperformed since Tuesday's election.
impact.layman: Big chip and AI companies fell the most. Safer places did better: Treasuries rose, and WSJ said home builders held up better since Tuesday's election.

outlook.technical: Base rates, not predictions: after S&P 500 falls bigger than 1 standard deviation of the previous 60 days, the next day rose 47% of 154 times and the next 5 days rose 58% of 153 times. Its 5 look-alike days saw the next 5 days rise 4 of 5 times (median 1.70%).
outlook.layman: Past patterns are not predictions. After similar big drops, the S&P 500 rose the next day 47% of 154 times, close to a coin flip. Over the next 5 days it rose 58% of 153 times.

regions.title: Americas: US tech rout, Mexico cuts, Brazil pauses

status.technical: On 2026-11-05 the S&P 500 closed -4.36%, Dow -3.44%, Russell 2000 -4.45% and TSX -2.03%; Reuters (via Mint) reported the steepest TSX decline in five months. Bloomberg reported Bank of Mexico unexpectedly cut to 6.25%; IPC 0.38%. WSJ reported Brazil's central bank held rates after five consecutive cuts; Bovespa -0.82%.
status.layman: US and Canadian stocks fell, and the tech-heavy Nasdaq was hit hardest. Mexico's central bank surprised markets by cutting its rate to 6.25%. Brazil's central bank paused after five cuts in a row.

consequence.technical: Bloomberg reported Banxico said it plans to hold at 6.25% going forward, so further cuts are not signalled. WSJ reported Brazil paused as inflation drifted away from target. Reuters (via Mint) attributed the TSX drop to the US tech rout.
consequence.layman: Mexico's bank says it plans to keep its rate at 6.25% from here. Brazil stopped cutting because inflation was drifting away from its target. Canadian shares fell along with US tech.

impact.technical: US equity holders, especially in tech, took the loss; Mexican borrowers face a lower benchmark rate; Brazil keeps steep rates. The notes give little detail on sector effects in Canada beyond the Reuters headline, so evidence there is thin.
impact.layman: US share owners, especially in tech, lost the most. Borrowers in Mexico get a lower benchmark rate. The notes say little else about Canada, so evidence is thin.

outlook.technical: Base rates, not predictions: after one-day falls bigger than 1 standard deviation, the Russell 2000 next 5 days rose 57% of 167 times (median 0.44%); its look-alike days saw the next 5 days rise 2 of 5 times (median -1.35%). The TSX next 5 days rose 55% of 172 times.
outlook.layman: Past patterns, not predictions. After similar drops, smaller US companies (Russell 2000) rose over the next 5 days 57% of 167 times. Its closest look-alike days were mixed: 2 of 5 rose.

regions.title: Europe: shares near August highs; BoE raises rates

status.technical: On their latest closes (2026-11-04) DAX rose 2.22%, CAC 40 1.96% and Euro Stoxx 50 1.97%; FTSE 100 closed -0.43% on 2026-11-05. Yahoo Finance UK reported European shares at their highest since August and the Bank of England raising rates. The FT reported the Stoxx Europe 600 is ahead of the S&P 500 this year.
status.layman: European shares rose to their highest level since August, said Yahoo Finance UK. The Bank of England raised interest rates. The FT said Europe now beats the US so far this year.

consequence.technical: Economic Times reported eurozone bond yields edged lower as oil prices stabilised, but rising inflation, potential ECB rate hikes and political uncertainty in France still shape sentiment. If oil stays stable, that easing backdrop could persist.
consequence.layman: Bond yields in the eurozone slipped as oil calmed down. But rising prices, possible ECB rate hikes and French politics still worry investors.

impact.technical: Euro-area savers and borrowers: the ECB main refinancing rate is 2.65% and the deposit rate 2.5% (ECB Data Portal). In the hand-kept Euro Stoxx 50 list, 7 of 9 rose on the day, while ASML fell -3.42%.
impact.layman: Euro-area rates are set by the ECB at 2.65% (main rate) and 2.5% for deposits. Most of Europe's biggest listed names rose, but chip equipment maker ASML fell.

outlook.technical: Base rates, not predictions: after one-day rises bigger than 1 standard deviation, the DAX next day rose 52% of 194 times and the next 5 days rose 56% of 193 times; its look-alike days saw the next 5 days rise 2 of 5 times (median -1.13%).
outlook.layman: Past patterns, not predictions. After similar big up days, the DAX rose the next day 52% of 194 times and over 5 days 56% of 193 times.

regions.title: Asia-Pacific: Korean chips slump, India rallies

status.technical: Mint reported the Kospi fell 5.3% as chip shares sold off, prompting temporary trading restrictions; Bloomberg reported Korean chip stocks sank 10% pre-market. Business Standard reported the Nifty rose 2.4% to 24,536.60 and the Sensex 2.6% on falling crude and foreign inflows. Latest closes: Nikkei 225 -1.42%, Hang Seng 1.67%, Shanghai 2.16%.
status.layman: Asia was split. South Korea's market fell about 5.3% as chip shares sold off. Indian shares jumped, helped by lower oil prices and foreign buying, said Business Standard.

consequence.technical: Bloomberg tied the Korean chip fears to how a Democratic Congress could slow AI infrastructure expansion. If that concern persists, Asian chip names stay exposed. Bloomberg also reported Japan's wage growth keeps the Bank of Japan on track to hike as soon as December, and Mint reported the yen rose on haven demand.
consequence.layman: Korean chip companies fell because investors fear a slower AI building boom. Japan's strong pay growth makes a rate rise there by December likelier, Bloomberg said. The yen rose as investors sought safety.

impact.technical: Economic Times reported emerging markets lost $33.8 billion in October as investors fled Asian stocks, mostly Taiwan. In the hand-kept Nikkei list Advantest fell -14.71% and Tokyo Electron -9.42%, while Hang Seng names Tencent (7.17%) and Alibaba (8.45%) rose.
impact.layman: Foreign investors pulled $33.8 billion out of emerging markets in October, mostly from Asian stocks. Japanese chip equipment makers fell sharply while big Chinese tech names rose.

outlook.technical: Base rates, not predictions: the Nikkei next 5 days rose 57% of 818 times after ordinary days; the Kospi next 5 days rose 57% of 823 times, and its look-alike days (only 5 cases) saw the next 5 days rise 4 of 5 times (median 5.98%).
outlook.layman: Past patterns, not predictions. After ordinary days, Japan's Nikkei rose over the next 5 days 57% of 818 times. South Korea's Kospi did the same 57% of 823 times.

status.technical: CNBC reported Democratic winners and progressive lawmakers are calling for tougher limits on AI and data centers, including a national moratorium. The FT reported newly elected officials have pledged to curb data centre construction. Bloomberg reported Rep. Subramanyam (D-VA) supports building data centers but believes a federal approach is needed.
status.layman: After the midterms, some Democrats want tougher rules on AI and data centres. One congressman said he supports data centres but wants a federal plan.

consequence.technical: If limits on data-centre construction advance, the AI infrastructure build-out could slow, which Bloomberg named as the fear behind the chip sell-off. The notes do not say what legislation will pass.
consequence.layman: If data-centre building is restricted, AI spending could slow. The notes do not say which rules, if any, will pass.

impact.technical: Chipmakers and AI infrastructure firms are most exposed per the notes: Bloomberg reported Korean chip stocks sinking 10% pre-market. CNBC reported Tesla and SpaceX lost over $420 billion in combined market cap after the midterms.
impact.layman: Chip and AI companies are most exposed. Tesla and SpaceX together lost over $420 billion in value, CNBC said.

outlook.technical: Base rates, not predictions: after Nasdaq falls bigger than 1 standard deviation, the next 5 days rose 54% of 169 times (median 0.26%, 10th-90th pct -3.89% to 4.53%).
outlook.layman: Past patterns, not predictions. After similar big Nasdaq drops, it rose over the next 5 days 54% of 169 times.

status.technical: CNBC reported neocloud IREN said $4 billion in annualized revenue is being delayed at a customer's request, and Bloomberg News (via Reuters) reported Microsoft is tightening oversight of neocloud data center projects. WSJ reported major investors are skeptical Anthropic's IPO can achieve a $1.5 Trillion valuation.
status.layman: Some AI infrastructure revenue is being pushed back, per CNBC. Microsoft is watching its data centre partners more closely. WSJ said big investors doubt a $1.5 Trillion valuation for Anthropic's IPO.

consequence.technical: If AI infrastructure customers keep delaying projects, revenues tied to the build-out could shift later, as IREN described. WSJ said Anthropic may need a significantly lower valuation than expected.
consequence.layman: If AI customers keep delaying projects, AI suppliers may book sales later. WSJ says Anthropic may need to set a lower price than hoped.

impact.technical: AI infrastructure suppliers and prospective AI IPO investors are affected, per WSJ, CNBC and Bloomberg. Evidence about wider effects is thin.
impact.layman: AI infrastructure suppliers and investors in future AI listings are the people affected. Evidence beyond that is thin.

outlook.technical: Base rates, not predictions: after Nasdaq falls bigger than 1 standard deviation, the next day rose 49% of 171 times; its look-alike days saw the next 21 days rise 4 of 5 times (median 5.46%).
outlook.layman: Past patterns, not predictions. After similar big Nasdaq drops, the next day was up 49% of 171 times.

status.technical: The VIX closed at 28.18, 69.66% higher on the day. Bloomberg reported the cost to hedge against the biggest S&P 500 plunge in more than a year soared; CNBC reported the intraday VIX range was more than 11 points. Mint reported Treasuries rose and the yen gained on haven demand; US 10-year yield closed at 4.84.
status.layman: The market's fear gauge (the VIX) jumped to 28.18. Traders paid much more for protection against further falls. Investors moved into safer assets like Treasuries and the yen.

consequence.technical: If selling continues, hedging costs may stay elevated. Historically the VIX has mean-reverted after spikes; CIBC and Nomura, per Mint, expect yen strength to continue.
consequence.layman: If the selling goes on, protection against falls stays costly. Two banks, CIBC and Nomura, expect the yen to keep rising, Mint reported.

impact.technical: Equity holders face larger swings; Treasury and yen holders benefited from haven demand. The notes do not detail effects on ordinary savers.
impact.layman: Share owners face bigger ups and downs. Holders of Treasuries and yen gained as safe assets. The notes say little about ordinary savers.

outlook.technical: Base rates, not predictions: after VIX one-day rises bigger than 1 standard deviation, the next day rose 39% of 174 times and the next 5 days rose 36% of 172 times; its look-alike days saw the next 21 days rise 0 of 5 times (median -21.43%).
outlook.layman: Past patterns, not predictions. After similar fear-gauge spikes, it rose again the next day only 39% of 174 times.

status.technical: Brent closed at 99.40, 5.05% higher on the day. Iran said five oil tankers and a tugboat caught fire in several incidents in the Strait of Hormuz (Al Jazeera). Economic Times reported US yields fell as oil rose. WSJ reported Qantas expects a $2.63 Billion first-half fuel bill and Straits Times said it will cut flying in Australia by 4%.
status.layman: Oil jumped to 99.40 a barrel for Brent. Iran says oil tankers caught fire near the Strait of Hormuz. Qantas says fuel costs are biting and will cut some flights.

consequence.technical: If Hormuz incidents persist, oil could stay elevated and airlines' fuel costs could stay high, as Qantas described. Economic Times reported investors reassessing US-Iran relations.
consequence.layman: If trouble near Hormuz continues, oil could stay expensive and airlines would keep feeling it, as Qantas shows.

impact.technical: Airlines such as Qantas are affected through fuel costs, per WSJ and Straits Times. Evidence for other sectors is thin.
impact.layman: Airlines pay more for fuel, and passengers may see higher fares, as Qantas did. The notes give little on other sectors.

outlook.technical: Base rates, not predictions: after Brent one-day rises bigger than 1 standard deviation, the next day rose 52% of 177 times and the next 5 days rose 46% of 176 times (10th-90th pct -7.58% to 7.58%).
outlook.layman: Past patterns, not predictions. After similar oil jumps, Brent rose the next day 52% of 177 times.

status.technical: Bloomberg reported Banxico cut to 6.25%, a four-year low, and Bank of England raised rates (Yahoo Finance UK). Bloomberg reported Japan's wages are on track to keep the BOJ on course to hike as soon as December. Uday Kotak expects another 50-75 basis points of RBI repo rate hikes (Business Standard). WSJ reported Brazil stopped easing.
status.layman: Central banks are going different ways. Mexico cut rates, the Bank of England raised them, and Brazil paused. Japan may raise rates in December, Bloomberg said.

consequence.technical: If Japanese wage momentum holds, Bloomberg expects the BOJ to hike as soon as December. Uday Kotak is quoted expecting more RBI repo hikes; this is his view, not an RBI statement.
consequence.layman: If Japanese pay keeps rising, a rate rise in December becomes likelier, per Bloomberg. Banker Uday Kotak personally expects more Indian rate rises.

impact.technical: Borrowers and savers in each country are affected; Freddie Mac reported the average US 30-year mortgage rate fell to 7.18%, a third straight decline (Economic Times).
impact.layman: Borrowers feel rate moves. In the US the average 30-year mortgage rate fell to 7.18% for a third week.

outlook.technical: Base rates, not predictions: after US 10-year yield one-day falls bigger than 1 standard deviation, the next 5 days rose 56% of 154 times (median 0.41%).
outlook.layman: Past patterns, not predictions. After similar yield drops, yields rose over the next 5 days 56% of 154 times.
